quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Bicycle store.
Soft shoulders.

questions.explanation: This sign shows where bicycles cross or ride. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles are likely to be present.

questions.question: This is a ____ sign.

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield
Do not enter

questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a "Yield" sign. Slow down and let other traffic and pedestrians pass. Stop only if necessary.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
You may not pass.
You may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot before changing lanes, driving away from a curb, or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: A driver going much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. On two-lane roads, pull over to let cars pass if traffic backs up behind you. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: When driving uphill behind a heavy truck, know that:

options.text: The truck may travel slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Passing on hills with poor visibility is against the law. Use caution when approaching trucks from behind.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against the light or being careless.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is present.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols indicate construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway ends.
One-way traffic ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Keep to the right.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the upcoming divider.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but there is heavy oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Go ahead because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for that traffic to pass before you turn. If the light is green and the path is clear, you may enter the intersection to prepare for your left turn.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may drive in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots regularly.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for road conditions. Always follow speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating can slow alcohol absorption but cannot prevent intoxication from drinking too much.

questions.question: Distracted drivers have a higher crash risk when using which of these?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving is dangerous. These distractions increase your crash risk.

questions.question: What affects your braking distance?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going
The condition of your brakes and tires
The condition of the road surface
All of the above

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view
When exiting a highway
When following a motorcycle
All of the above

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting a highway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who doesn't follow traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always receive a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When pulling out of a driveway onto a street, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly so vehicles and pedestrians can move out of your way.
Honk your horn so vehicles and pedestrians know to move.
Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians. The stop must be made before the sidewalk. Failure to stop is against the law.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is letting out children, you should:

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: If your tire blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake gently.
Press the accelerator.
Turn quickly off the road.
Hit the brakes and stop as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down by releasing the accelerator and using the brakes gently. Move off the road to a safe place when you can.

questions.question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with siren and/or flashing lights approaches you?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with lights or sirens, move your car to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: If you feel worried, nervous, angry, or upset, you should:

options.text: Drive normally as usual.
Drive faster because you are more alert.
Calm down and focus on driving before you start the car.
Call a friend to talk while you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus on driving before you start the car.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness make it hard to drive safely. Your mind becomes distracted from driving. Take time to relax and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the side of the road and empty.
When it approaches you, even if the lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus has red lights flashing while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, cars from both directions must stop while the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is out.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is open.
If no right lane exists, wait for clear road ahead and slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If a car is tailgating you, move to the right lane if one is available. If not, wait until the road ahead is clear and slow down gradually. This lets the tailgater pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a crash.
